anatomy.intro: One mother rosette can produce daughter rosettes on visible connecting stolons.

parts.label: Fleshy leaf

parts.function: New leaves emerge at the growing center.
parts.label: Rosette center

parts.function: This slender stem extends outward to a developing daughter rosette.
parts.label: Stolon

parts.function: An offset can root and become another independent crown.

flowers.text: A mature Sempervivum rosette elongates into a flower stalk that can reach about 1 ft, topped with star-shaped blooms. Mountain Crest Gardens lists pink flowers for 'Coconut Crystal'. The flowering rosette dies afterward; its offsets continue the colony.

growth.note: A rosette can produce offsets for years before its center rises into a flowering stem.

stages.text: The rosette expands with tightly arranged leaves.
stages.title: Build a crown

stages.text: Stolons carry small offsets around the original crown.
stages.title: Send out chicks

stages.text: A flowering crown dies afterward; surviving offsets continue the colony.
stages.title: Flower and renew

habitat.text: 'Coconut Crystal' is a garden selection of hens-and-chicks. The genus favors open, rocky, freely draining places and benefits from cool nights and a cold dormant season. Its low rosettes spread through offsets on slender stolons, gradually filling gaps around the original crown.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria 'Raindrops'
lookalikes.text: Both make fleshy rosettes, but hens-and-chicks spreads on stolons and loses each crown after flowering; 'Raindrops' is recognized by rounded leaf bumps and produces few offsets.

mature.text: Mountain Crest Gardens lists foliage under 3 inches high and rosettes up to 5–6 inches across. A colony can spread farther through offsets, so its total footprint differs from the width of one rosette.

nameStory.text: Sempervivum means 'forever alive': replacement offsets make a colony seem permanent even though a flowering rosette is not. Mountain Crest Gardens attributes 'Coconut Crystal' to Gielis.
